subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: For `p = base + index + K` where base is a pointer local, index an integer local and K a compile-time constant, MWCC decides the operand grouping BEFORE codegen and no spelling of the SAME expression can change it: it emits `addi rT,index,K` then `add rP,base,rT`, and both parenthesisation (`(base + index) + K`) and commutative operand order (`index + base + K`) are byte-identical no-ops. The grouping flips to the target-side form — `add rP,base,index` then a displacement load `lwz rD,(K+F)(rP)` then `addi rP,rP,K` — ONLY when the base sum acquires a CONSUMER standing between the sum and the pointer's completion, and it takes all three of these together: (a) the consumer must be rooted at the base sum with the constant folded into ONE literal, i.e. `*(T*)(slot + (K + F))`, not `*(T*)(p + F)` and not `*(T*)(base + index + K + F)` (the latter re-exposes `base + index + K` as a subexpression and CSE simply rebuilds the pointer); (b) the consumer must stand BEFORE the pointer's completion in source order, or MWCC materialises the pointer first and keeps two registers live; (c) the pointer must be a DISTINCT variable assigned from the base local (`p = slot + K`), never a self-update of it (`p = slot; ...; p += K`) — the self-update is value-numbered back to `slot + K` and folded into every later use, deleting the `addi` and converting every downstream `mr rN,rP` into `addi rN,slot,K`. Measured on do_player_select at ten sites: the three-part form closed thirteen multiset tokens to nine and moved fuzzy 96.6218 -> 97.6578, while (a) alone read 96.5560, (a)+(b) without (c) read 96.3241 with four instructions LOST, and the two neutral spelling probes were byte-identical.
